infrastructure.air_passengers.plain: How many passengers board a commercial flight at the airports of each municipality, every year.
infrastructure.air_passengers.plain_es: Cuántos pasajeros abordan un vuelo comercial en los aeropuertos de cada municipio, cada año.
infrastructure.air_passengers.definition: Passengers who boarded a commercial flight at an airport in the municipality during the year, to anywhere: the US mainland, another island or abroad. A passenger is counted each time they board.
infrastructure.air_passengers.method: gateway_series.py sums BTS's monthly T-100 rows of the seven Puerto Rico airports in the file (SJU, BQN, PSE, VQS, CPX, SIG, MAZ) by year, and places each airport in the municipality that holds it (the FAA airports of transport.json): San Juan's Luis Muñoz Marín (SJU) is in Carolina and Isla Grande (SIG) in San Juan. A year is published once SJU has all twelve months.
infrastructure.air_passengers.how_to_read: 7.2 million passengers boarded at Puerto Rico's airports in 2025, 6.7 million of them at SJU (Carolina); in 2020 the figure fell to 2.5 million.
caveats: Counts boardings, not visitors: residents travelling and passengers changing planes are counted, and a passenger who arrives is not.
Ceiba's airport (RVR) is not in T-100; see the FAA count.
A smaller airport with fewer months in a year had no commercial flights in the others (Ponce reported 3 months in 2020 and 9 in 2021).
infrastructure.air_passengers.source_detail: BTS T-100 Segment Summary by Origin Airport (data.bts.gov r495-tyji): total_passengers by origin_airport_code and month

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: air passengers boarding (commercial flights)

infrastructure.air_enplanements_faa.plain: How many passengers board at the commercial airports of each municipality, as FAA counts them.
infrastructure.air_enplanements_faa.plain_es: Cuántos pasajeros abordan en los aeropuertos comerciales de cada municipio, según los cuenta la FAA.
infrastructure.air_enplanements_faa.definition: Passengers who boarded at a commercial service airport in the municipality during the calendar year, as FAA counts them for airport funding. It includes Ceiba's airport (RVR) and on-demand air taxi flights.
infrastructure.air_enplanements_faa.method: gateway_series.py reads every FAA file under its current name (CY2024 and CY2025, which give 2023 to 2025) and keeps Puerto Rico's rows; for a year two files share, the file of that year wins. Each airport is placed in its municipality as for T-100.
infrastructure.air_enplanements_faa.how_to_read: FAA counted 7.19 million boardings in 2025, within 0.1% of T-100's 7.20 million; Ceiba's 23,214 are only here.
caveats: Earlier years are in files under other names that no longer answer; the series starts in 2023.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: air passengers boarding (faa enplanements)

infrastructure.air_departures.plain: How many commercial flights leave the airports of each municipality, every year.
infrastructure.air_departures.plain_es: Cuántos vuelos comerciales salen de los aeropuertos de cada municipio, cada año.
infrastructure.air_departures.definition: Commercial flights, passenger and cargo, that departed from an airport in the municipality during the year.
infrastructure.air_departures.method: gateway_series.py sums BTS's monthly T-100 rows of the seven Puerto Rico airports in the file (SJU, BQN, PSE, VQS, CPX, SIG, MAZ) by year, and places each airport in the municipality that holds it (the FAA airports of transport.json): San Juan's Luis Muñoz Marín (SJU) is in Carolina and Isla Grande (SIG) in San Juan. A year is published once SJU has all twelve months.
infrastructure.air_departures.how_to_read: 94,613 commercial flights left Puerto Rico's airports in 2025, 68,110 of them from SJU.
caveats: Small island flights (Vieques, Culebra) carry few passengers each, so flights and passengers rank the airports differently.
infrastructure.air_departures.source_detail: BTS T-100 Segment Summary by Origin Airport (data.bts.gov r495-tyji): total_departures by origin_airport_code and month

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: commercial flights departing

infrastructure.ferry_passengers.plain: How many passengers board a ferry at the terminals of each municipality, in the years of the ferry census.
infrastructure.ferry_passengers.plain_es: Cuántos pasajeros abordan una lancha en los terminales de cada municipio, en los años del censo de lanchas.
infrastructure.ferry_passengers.definition: Passengers who boarded a ferry at a terminal in the municipality during the year the census covers, as the operator reported them: the Cataño crossing (Cataño and Old San Juan), Ceiba, Vieques and Culebra. Passengers going and coming back are each counted where they board.
infrastructure.ferry_passengers.method: gateway_series.py reads each census's terminals in Puerto Rico, the one-way segments that start at them and the operator's passengers on each segment. A segment's passengers board at its first terminal, which is placed in the municipality that holds its point. The 2020 census gives data year 2019; since 2022 BTS names each census for the year of its data. The 2018 census is left out: it does not state its data year and its routes start at Fajardo, before the move to Ceiba.
infrastructure.ferry_passengers.how_to_read: 1.62 million ferry boardings in 2024: 593,000 at Ceiba, 321,000 at Vieques, 273,000 at Culebra and 429,000 on the Cataño crossing.
caveats: Reported by the operator to the census, not counted by the observatory.
Only three years; the year control shows the latest census at or before the year chosen.
2022 was a year of reduced service on the Cataño crossing (84,145 and 86,441 boardings).
infrastructure.ferry_passengers.source_detail: BTS NCFO operator segment, segment and terminal files of 2020, 2022 and 2024 (data.bts.gov): passengers, trips_per_year, seg_terminal1_id, terminal points

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: ferry passengers boarding

transit.airport_city.plain: The city the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) associates with the airport. It can differ from the municipality where the airport lies.
transit.airport_city.plain_es: La ciudad que la FAA (Administración Federal de Aviación) asocia con el aeropuerto. Puede ser distinta del municipio donde está el aeropuerto.
transit.airport_city.definition: City name from the FAA record, in title case. In the 2026-10 snapshot there are 13 different values among 14 airports; examples are Isla De Culebra and Isla De Vieques. Only FAA airports have it.
transit.airport_city.method: Copied from the FAA field city and converted to title case.
caveats: The city is an address label, not a boundary. Use the municipality field for counts by municipality.
transit.airport_city.source_detail: FAA Aviation Facilities layer 0 of the National Transportation Atlas Database, state_post_office_code=PR, field city

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

transit.airport_code.plain: The short code the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) gives the airport. It is not always the same as the airline code of the International Air Transport Association (IATA).
transit.airport_code.plain_es: El código corto que la FAA (Administración Federal de Aviación) le da al aeropuerto. No siempre es igual al código de aerolíneas de la IATA (Asociación Internacional de Transporte Aéreo).
transit.airport_code.definition: FAA location identifier, 3 or 4 characters (examples from the 2026-10 snapshot: SJU, BQN, X63, PR20). In the 2026-10 snapshot there are 14 different values, one per FAA airport. Only FAA airports have it.
transit.airport_code.method: Copied from the FAA field loc_id.
caveats: Private-use airports have codes such as PR20 or 02PR that are not airline codes.
For the airline code (IATA) and the aviation code of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), see the separate field entry; they are not filled for FAA airports.
transit.airport_code.source_detail: FAA Aviation Facilities layer 0 of the National Transportation Atlas Database, state_post_office_code=PR, field loc_id

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

transit.airport_iata_icao.plain: Two airport codes that volunteers can add in OpenStreetMap: the 3-letter code of the International Air Transport Association (IATA), used by airlines, and the 4-letter code of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). Only one airport, in Fajardo, has them in the 2026-10 snapshot.
transit.airport_iata_icao.plain_es: Dos códigos de aeropuerto que las personas voluntarias pueden agregar en OpenStreetMap: el código de 3 letras de la IATA (Asociación Internacional de Transporte Aéreo), que usan las aerolíneas, y el código de 4 letras de la ICAO (Organización de Aviación Civil Internacional). En el corte de datos de 2026-10, solo un aeropuerto, en Fajardo, los tiene.
transit.airport_iata_icao.definition: Text from the OpenStreetMap (OSM) tags iata (3 letters) and icao (4 letters). In the 2026-10 snapshot they are present on one record: Aeropuerto Diego Jiménez Torres in Fajardo (FAJ, TJFA). They are null on the other OSM points and absent from scheduled stops and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airports.
transit.airport_iata_icao.method: Copied from the OSM tags when present.
caveats: Null means not recorded here. It does not mean the airport has no IATA or ICAO code: the FAA records do not carry these fields, so even the main San Juan airport has none here (use the FAA code field).

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

transit.airport_public_use.plain: True when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lists the airport as public use, false when it is private use. Only FAA airports have it.
transit.airport_public_use.plain_es: Verdadero cuando la FAA (Administración Federal de Aviación) clasifica el aeropuerto como de uso público, falso cuando es de uso privado. Solo lo tienen los aeropuertos de la FAA.
transit.airport_public_use.definition: True when the FAA facility-use code is PU (public use); false for PR (private use). In the 2026-10 snapshot the field is present on the 14 FAA airports (10 public, 4 private). The 11 aerodromes mapped in OpenStreetMap (OSM) do not have the field.
transit.airport_public_use.method: transport.py compares the FAA field fac_use to PU.
caveats: True when the FAA record's use code is PU and false when it is PR, as the FAA lists them; see the FAA source for its definitions. It does not mean airline service exists.

The map popup shows Public use for any airport without this field, so in the 2026-10 snapshot the 11 OSM-mapped aerodromes (one of them marked closed in its name) read as Public use on the map even though the data do not say so.
transit.airport_public_use.source_detail: FAA Aviation Facilities layer 0 of the National Transportation Atlas Database, state_post_office_code=PR, field fac_use

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

municipalities.airports.plain: How many airports and airfields lie inside the municipality, from the list of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and from OpenStreetMap. It includes small, private, historic and seaplane facilities.
municipalities.airports.plain_es: Cuántos aeropuertos y aeródromos hay dentro del municipio, según la lista de la FAA (Administración Federal de Aviación) y OpenStreetMap. Incluye instalaciones pequeñas, privadas, históricas y para hidroaviones.
municipalities.airports.definition: Count of airport features inside the municipality: the Puerto Rico airports in the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) list, public and private use, plus OpenStreetMap features tagged aeroway=aerodrome that lie 2 km or more from every FAA airport. Helipads are not counted.
municipalities.airports.method: FAA airports with state code PR come from the BTS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics) NTAD (National Transportation Atlas Database). OpenStreetMap aerodromes less than 2 km from an FAA airport are treated as the same airport and dropped. Each remaining feature is assigned to the municipality whose boundary contains it.
municipalities.airports.how_to_read: The count is of facilities, not of airlines or flights, and it is not a rate. A value of 1 can mean a large commercial airport or a small airfield. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 25 airports: 14 from the FAA list and 11 from OpenStreetMap. Overture Maps also lists 120 places under its airport category in the 2026-10 snapshot; that is a count of place listings, not of airports (see places.type.transportation).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the OpenStreetMap aerodromes include seaplane bases, historic and military airfields, and one whose name says it is closed (Patillas, marked CERRADO). They all count.

Counts follow the map pin, not the FAA city: in the 2026-10 snapshot Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport is listed under San Juan by the FAA but its coordinates fall in Carolina, so Carolina counts it.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.
municipalities.airports.source_detail: FAA airports via BTS NTAD (layer Airports_, state code PR; list downloaded 1 October 2026, 14 airports); OpenStreetMap aeroway=aerodrome (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)

view.label: Map, Municipality tab (click a municipality): Mobility section
Map, Map layers tab: Stations, terminals & airports
3D + Time page: municipality popup (airports)

municipalities.ev_charging.plain: How many electric-vehicle (EV) charging points volunteers have mapped in OpenStreetMap inside the municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island total is only 11, so a 0 does not show that the municipality has no chargers.
municipalities.ev_charging.plain_es: Cuántos puntos de carga de vehículos eléctricos han registrado personas voluntarias en OpenStreetMap dentro del municipio. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 el total de la isla es de solo 11, así que un 0 no demuestra que el municipio no tenga cargadores.
municipalities.ev_charging.definition: Count of OpenStreetMap points tagged amenity=charging_station inside the municipality. Only points are read, not areas. It counts mapped points, not plugs or chargers.
municipalities.ev_charging.method: The build queries OpenStreetMap through the Overpass API (application programming interface) for points tagged amenity=charging_station, assigns each to the municipality whose boundary contains it and counts them. Nothing is merged or removed.
municipalities.ev_charging.how_to_read: Use it only as a rough sign of where charging has been mapped. It is not an inventory of chargers. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island total is 11: Carolina 4, Guaynabo 4, Aguadilla 1, Mayagüez 1 and Lares 1.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot only 11 points are mapped island-wide, so treat the count as mapping effort, not as an inventory. The observatory holds no reference count to say how complete it is. One site mapped as several points counts several times: in that snapshot Guaynabo has three points with the same name.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.
municipalities.ev_charging.source_detail: OpenStreetMap amenity=charging_station (nodes; extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)

view.label: Map, Municipality tab (click a municipality): Mobility section
Map, Map layers tab: Taxi stands & EV charging

municipalities.taxi_stands.plain: How many taxi stands volunteers have mapped in OpenStreetMap inside the municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island total is only 9, so a 0 does not show that the municipality has no taxi stands.
municipalities.taxi_stands.plain_es: Cuántas paradas de taxis han registrado personas voluntarias en OpenStreetMap dentro del municipio. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 el total de la isla es de solo 9, así que un 0 no demuestra que el municipio no tenga paradas de taxis.
municipalities.taxi_stands.definition: Count of OpenStreetMap points tagged amenity=taxi inside the municipality. Only points are read, not areas.
municipalities.taxi_stands.method: The build queries OpenStreetMap through the Overpass API (application programming interface) for points tagged amenity=taxi, assigns each to the municipality whose boundary contains it and counts them. Nothing is merged or removed.
municipalities.taxi_stands.how_to_read: Treat it as a sign of mapping effort as much as of taxi service. A 0 does not mean there are no taxis. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island total is 9: San Juan 6, Arecibo 1, Caguas 1 and Aguadilla 1. Overture Maps lists 28 places in its taxi service category in the 2026-10 snapshot (see places.type.transportation); that is a different count from mapped stands.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot only 9 points are mapped island-wide, so treat the count as mapping effort, not as an inventory. The observatory holds no reference count to say how complete it is. Ride-share pickup zones tagged as taxi stands also appear in the data.
Counts points, so one stand mapped twice counts twice.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.
municipalities.taxi_stands.source_detail: OpenStreetMap amenity=taxi (nodes; extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)

view.label: Map, Municipality tab (click a municipality): Mobility section
Map, Map layers tab: Taxi stands & EV charging

municipalities.public_airports.plain: How many of the municipality's airports the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lists as open to the public. Airports known only from OpenStreetMap are not counted here.
municipalities.public_airports.plain_es: Cuántos de los aeropuertos del municipio aparecen en la lista de la FAA (Administración Federal de Aviación) como abiertos al público. Los aeropuertos que solo se conocen por OpenStreetMap no se cuentan aquí.
municipalities.public_airports.definition: Count of FAA airports inside the municipality whose FAA use code is PU (public use). It is a subset of airports. Airports with the FAA use code PR (private use) are not counted as public use.
municipalities.public_airports.method: The build sets a public-use flag for each FAA record when its use code (fac_use) equals PU, then counts flagged airports per municipality. OpenStreetMap aerodromes carry no such flag in this dataset and are never counted.
municipalities.public_airports.how_to_read: Use it to see where the FAA lists an airport open to the public. It does not say whether airlines serve it. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 10 public-use airports among its 14 FAA airports; the other four (in Adjuntas, Cabo Rojo, Lajas and Vega Baja) are private use.
caveats: An airport known only from OpenStreetMap is not counted because its record has no public-use flag. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Fajardo's Aeropuerto Diego Jiménez Torres (code FAJ) is in the data only through OpenStreetMap, because the FAA list the observatory uses does not include it, so Fajardo shows 2 airports and 0 public ones.
The value follows the FAA list at the date of the build; the FAA can change a facility's status.
municipalities.public_airports.source_detail: FAA airports via BTS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics) NTAD (National Transportation Atlas Database), field fac_use = PU; list downloaded 1 October 2026; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)

view.label: Map, Municipality tab (click a municipality): Mobility section

transit.taxi_ev_charging.plain: Taxi stands and electric vehicle chargers that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap (OSM). The 2026-10 snapshot has 9 taxi stands and 11 chargers.
transit.taxi_ev_charging.plain_es: Paradas de taxis y cargadores de vehículos eléctricos que personas voluntarias mapearon en OpenStreetMap (OSM). El corte de datos de 2026-10 tiene 9 paradas de taxis y 11 cargadores.
transit.taxi_ev_charging.definition: OSM points tagged amenity=taxi (kind taxi) and amenity=charging_station (kind ev_charging). The 2026-10 snapshot has 9 taxi points and 11 charging points. The data carry a name, an operator tag and the municipality; they do not record the number of plugs, the power, the price, opening hours or whether the charger is working. The map layer also reserves bike_rental and helipad; the 2026-10 snapshot has no such points.
transit.taxi_ev_charging.method: Read from OpenStreetMap by transport.py with the other mapped points.
transit.taxi_ev_charging.how_to_read: Use the layer to see where such points are known. It is not a list of all taxis or chargers.
caveats: The list is whatever volunteers mapped; it is likely incomplete.
Taxi stands and chargers are not scheduled transit and are not counted in the transit stop totals.

layers.bridges.plain: Every bridge of 20 feet or more on a public road and the four road tunnels, from FHWA's inventories: the colour is the bridge's condition and the area of each circle is the vehicles that cross it on an average day.
layers.bridges.plain_es: Todos los puentes de 20 pies o más en una vía pública y los cuatro túneles de carretera, según los inventarios de la FHWA: el color es la condición del puente y el área de cada círculo, los vehículos que lo cruzan en un día promedio.
layers.bridges.definition: bridges.geojson: one point per bridge in the National Bridge Inventory of 2025 (2,426 bridges in the 78 municipios; 8 more have a point outside every municipio and are left out) and per tunnel in the National Tunnel Inventory (4). Each point has name (the road carried), type (Bridge or Tunnel), municipio, geoid, sn (structure or tunnel number), x (the feature crossed, or the road a tunnel carries), c (condition: G good, F fair, P poor, T a tunnel), lr (the lowest of the deck, superstructure, substructure or culvert ratings, 0-9), y (year built), yr (year rebuilt), a (average daily traffic) and ay (its year), t (trucks, % of traffic), d (detour if closed, km), l (length, m), o (status: A open, P posted for load, B should be posted, E or D open with temporary support, K closed), s (1 when scour critical, NBI item 113 codes 0-3), i (last inspection, YYYY-MM) and w (owner: state, toll, municipal, federal, other).
layers.bridges.method: transport_inventories.py reads the newest Puerto Rico file of the National Bridge Inventory (records of type 1, one per bridge), turns items 16 and 17 (degrees, minutes, seconds) into a point and places it in the municipio whose outline holds it; it adds the four tunnels of the National Tunnel Inventory (NTAD) at their portal. The condition is FHWA's own (BRIDGE_CONDITION, from the lowest rating). The map draws each circle with an area in proportion to the daily traffic (a radius of 0.024 times its square root, in pixels, at least 2.5); a closed bridge is drawn hollow. The file is sorted busiest first, so the quieter bridges are drawn on top.
layers.bridges.how_to_read: Switch the layer on in the Layers tab of the 2D map or the 3D view (Infrastructure and mobility: Mobility and transit). Dark red circles are bridges in poor condition; the largest circles carry the most traffic, on PR-18, PR-22 and PR-52 in the San Juan area. Click a bridge for its condition, any load limit, scour, year built, detour and last inspection. In 2025: 411 bridges in good condition, 1,671 fair and 344 poor; 24 closed and 695 posted or to be posted for load; 505 scour critical.
caveats: Poor does not mean unsafe: a bridge that is not safe is closed. Poor means a part rated 4 or below needs repair or closer watch.
Most traffic counts are from 2017; the pop-up gives each count's year.
The points are FHWA's coordinates; a few fall slightly off the road. Eight bridges with a point outside every municipio are left out.
layers.bridges.source_detail: NBI delimited file PR25.txt: STRUCTURE_NUMBER_008, RECORD_TYPE_005A, FEATURES_DESC_006A, FACILITY_CARRIED_007, LAT_016, LONG_017, DETOUR_KILOS_019, OWNER_022, YEAR_BUILT_027, ADT_029, YEAR_ADT_030, OPEN_CLOSED_POSTED_041, STRUCTURE_LEN_MT_049, DATE_OF_INSPECT_090, YEAR_RECONSTRUCTED_106, PERCENT_ADT_TRUCK_109, SCOUR_CRITICAL_113, BRIDGE_CONDITION, LOWEST_RATING; NTAD National Tunnel Inventory (state 72).

3D view, Layers tab: Bridges and tunnels

infrastructure.transit_links.plain: How many workers travel between each pair of municipios, and whether a bus, train or ferry route with a published timetable, or a público route on the 2020 list, joins the two. It shows where many people travel and no timetabled route is listed.
infrastructure.transit_links.plain_es: Cuántas personas viajan entre cada par de municipios para trabajar, y si una ruta de guagua, tren o lancha con horario publicado, o una ruta de públicos de la lista de 2020, une los dos. Muestra dónde viaja mucha gente y no aparece una ruta con horario.
infrastructure.transit_links.definition: transit_links.json: pairs lists every pair of municipios with workers travelling between them (columns in pair_fields): a, b (GEOIDs), ab, ba (workers who live in a and work in b, and the reverse), workers (the two added), moe (the 90 percent margin of error of the sum), low (the margin is as large as the estimate), status (timetable: a route with a current timetable has stops in both; expired: only routes whose timetable expired; publico: only a público route of the 2020 list; none), via (no direct route, but timetabled routes join the pair through other municipios), tt_routes, tt_trips (weekday trips of those routes), tt_ops (their operators), publicos (routes of the 2020 list that join the pair), km and min (the fastest road path between the two town centres and its driving time without traffic), sim (the pair's place among the simulated connections), aadt_med and aadt_max (for a simulated connection, the median and the highest annual average daily traffic of the counted main roads within 25 m of points every 100 m along its line; FHWA HPMS) and counted_pct (the share of those points on a counted road), tt_best, tt_typ and tt_xfers (the fastest trip by the weekday timetables between the two town centres, in either direction, leaving every 15 minutes from 6:00 to 9:00, in minutes; the median over those departures, waiting included; and the transfers on the fastest), tt_why (when there is no trip: 1, a town centre has no stop of the weekday timetables within 1 km; 2, no trip within 3 hours), along_res and along_far (for a simulated connection, the 2020 Census residents of the blocks within 1 km of its line, and those of them beyond 400 m in a straight line of a scheduled stop), bridges_poor and bridges_closed (bridges of the National Bridge Inventory within 50 m of its line in poor condition, or closed). municipios lists the 78 (muni_fields): resident_workers, work_elsewhere and work_elsewhere_pct, come_in, top_dest and top_dest_workers, linked_pct (the share of the workers travelling in or out who do so between pairs with a timetabled route), linked_pairs, sim_links, own_system (the state of the timetable of the municipio's own system), no_vehicle_pct and poverty_pct (households with no vehicle and residents below the poverty level, American Community Survey 2020-2024) and stop_km (straight-line km from the town centre to the nearest stop with weekday service). pr holds Puerto Rico's totals by status, and deaths_5y and walk_bike_5y (the people killed, and the pedestrians and bicyclists among them, in fatal crashes within 100 m of a simulated connection over 2020-2024; NHTSA FARS; five-year totals only).
infrastructure.transit_links.method: transit_links.py adds the two directions of each pair in the Census Bureau's County-to-County Commuting Flows (the margin of the sum is the root of the sum of the squares). A timetabled link is a route with stops (transport.json) in both municipios in trips.json, trips_sa.json or trips_su.json; for a municipal route whose trips time only their first and last stop, the operator's stops within 35 m of the route's line (transit_routes.geojson) count as its stops. It is current when the operator's timetable still runs (operators.json). A público route joins the municipios where its line ends and those whose town centre it passes within 1 km. Road paths are the fastest between town centres (gazetteer.json) on roads.bin, at the planner's speeds by kind of road. Checks that stop the build: the flows table must be the 2016-2020 release and cover the 78 municipios; every municipio must have a town centre and a road within 1 km of it; the público file must have its four columns. Journey times (step 5 of the upgrade, docs/transit-links.md): a connection scan over the weekday trips of trips.json, walking up to 1 km from and to the town centres and up to 400 m between stops (straight line times 1.3 at 1.2 m/s, plus 2 minutes a transfer). Municipal systems that time only the ends of their trips lose the trips that board or leave at their other stops.
infrastructure.transit_links.how_to_read: 532,691 of 1,000,096 workers (53.3%) work in a municipio other than the one where they live. A route with a current timetable joins 22 of the 1,084 pairs, which carry 26.8% of those workers; 34.5% travel between pairs with only a público route on the 2020 list, 36.5% between pairs with no route listed and 2.2% between 6 pairs whose only timetable expired.
caveats: Only work trips are counted: not trips to study, to a doctor or to shop, and not people without a job.
Workers are survey estimates of 2016-2020 with margins of error; small flows are unreliable (the field low marks them).
Públicos run without timetables, and the 2020 list has not been updated: a pair with no timetabled route is not a pair with no service.
Only direct routes count as a timetabled link; no journey time with transfers is computed.
A timetable shows the service an operator publishes, not the service that ran.
infrastructure.transit_links.geography: The 78 municipios and the 1,084 pairs of municipios with workers travelling between them
infrastructure.transit_links.source_detail: US Census Bureau, County-to-County Commuting Flows, ACS 2016-2020, Table 1 (https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/demo/tables/metro-micro/2020/commuting-flows-2020/table1.xlsx); Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico and ACT, Mapa de rutas de porteadores públicos (2020-03-19); the observatory's timetable files (ATI and municipal GTFS feeds) and road graph (OpenStreetMap).

layers.publicos.plain: A map layer with the público routes that were listed as active in March 2020, each with its code and name. The list has no timetable and has not been updated, so a route may no longer run.
layers.publicos.plain_es: Una capa del mapa con las rutas de públicos que aparecían activas en marzo de 2020, cada una con su código y su nombre. La lista no tiene horarios y no se ha actualizado, así que una ruta puede que ya no opere.
layers.publicos.definition: publicos.geojson: one line per route of the list, with type (between municipios or within a municipio), code (the route's code on the list), name and municipio (the municipios the route joins: where its line ends and those whose town centre it passes within 1 km).
layers.publicos.method: transit_links.py reads the CSV of the Instituto de Estadísticas (361 rows), joins the rows of one code into one route (the list gives some routes as two directions or as pieces), and simplifies the lines to 12 m. Nothing else is changed.
layers.publicos.how_to_read: Each line is a route as it was listed in 2020. Click it for its code, its name and the municipios it joins. Compare it with the Transit routes layer, which shows the routes with a published timetable.
caveats: The list is of March 2020: a route may no longer run, and routes that began later are missing.
No timetable, fares or operator: the layer says where a route was listed, not when it runs.
The lines are as the list drew them; some routes are drawn in pieces.
layers.publicos.geography: 334 routes; 147 join two municipios or more
layers.publicos.source_detail: Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico, open data portal, Mapa de rutas de porteadores públicos, with data of the Autoridad de Carreteras y Transportación (https://datos.estadisticas.pr/dataset/mapa-de-rutas-de-porteadores-publicos), published 2020-03-19, Creative Commons Attribution.

layers.transit_links.plain: A map layer with a dashed line for each pair of municipios where 500 or more workers travel between them and no timetabled transit route joins them. It is a simulation that shows where a connection is missing, not a proposed route.
layers.transit_links.plain_es: Una capa del mapa con una línea entrecortada por cada par de municipios entre los que viajan 500 personas o más para trabajar y que ninguna ruta de transporte colectivo con horario une. Es una simulación que muestra dónde falta una conexión, no una ruta propuesta.
layers.transit_links.definition: simulated_links.geojson: one line per simulated connection, with type, c (1: no route listed; 2: a público route joined the pair on the 2020 list), rank (1 is the pair with the most workers), name, a and b (the municipios), workers and moe (American Community Survey 2016-2020, both directions), km and min (the fastest road path between the two town centres and its driving time without traffic), publicos (routes of the 2020 list), via (timetabled routes join the pair with a transfer in another municipio), geoid_a and geoid_b, and aadt_med, aadt_max and counted_pct (the traffic on the counted main roads it follows: median, highest, and the share of its length on a counted road; FHWA HPMS), and deaths_5y and walk_bike_5y (the people killed, and the pedestrians and bicyclists among them, in fatal crashes within 100 m of a simulated connection over 2020-2024; NHTSA FARS; five-year totals only), along_res, along_far and bridges_poor (the residents within 1 km of its line, those of them beyond 400 m of a scheduled stop, and the bridges in poor condition within 50 m; 2020 Census, FHWA NBI), and tt_best or tt_why (the fastest trip by the weekday timetables between the two town centres, or why there is none).
layers.transit_links.method: transit_links.py draws a line for each pair with 500 workers or more, a margin of error smaller than the estimate and no timetabled route (current or expired). The line is the fastest path on the observatory's road graph (roads.bin, OpenStreetMap) between the two town centres, simplified to 12 m. The maps draw it wider where more workers travel.
layers.transit_links.how_to_read: Each dashed line joins two town centres along the roads. Orange: no route is listed for the pair (81 lines). Purple: a público route joined the pair on the 2020 list (101 lines). A thicker line means more workers travel between the two municipios. Click a line for the figures.
caveats: A simulation to show where a connection is missing: not a proposed route, a service plan or a demand forecast.
The line runs between town centres; where a real route would run, stop or end is not studied here.
Only work trips are counted, from a survey of 2016-2020 with margins of error.
Públicos run without timetables: a pair on this layer may have service.
layers.transit_links.geography: 182 pairs of municipios on the main island
layers.transit_links.source_detail: Simulated by Foundation for Puerto Rico from the Census Bureau's commuting flows (ACS 2016-2020), the published timetables of the ATI and the municipal systems, the público routes of the 2020 list and OpenStreetMap roads.

layers.evcharge.plain: The public electric vehicle charging stations in the US Department of Energy's Alternative Fuels Data Center: the area of each circle is the charging ports, and green means the station has DC fast charging.
layers.evcharge.plain_es: Las estaciones públicas de carga de vehículos eléctricos del Centro de Datos de Combustibles Alternativos del Departamento de Energía de EE. UU.: el área de cada círculo es la cantidad de puertos de carga, y el verde indica que la estación tiene carga rápida de corriente continua.
layers.evcharge.definition: ev_stations.geojson: one point per public electric charging station in the Alternative Fuels Data Center that is open or temporarily unavailable (26 on 2026-11-14 in 16 municipios, 53 ports, 2 stations with DC fast charging, 5 temporarily unavailable). Each point has name, type, municipio, geoid, afdc (the station id), kind (dc: has DC fast charging; l2: Level 2 only), ports (all ports), dc, l2 and l1 (ports by level), net (the charging network), conn (connector types), status (open or unavailable) and confirmed (the date the Department last confirmed it). The station's telephone and address are not kept.
layers.evcharge.method: transport_inventories.py reads the NTAD copy of the Alternative Fuels Data Center stations for Puerto Rico (fuel type ELEC, public access, status open or temporarily unavailable; no key) and places each station in the municipio whose outline holds it. The map draws each circle with an area in proportion to the ports (a radius of 3.7 times their square root, in pixels, at least 3.5); a station temporarily unavailable is drawn hollow.
layers.evcharge.how_to_read: Switch the layer on in the Layers tab of the 2D map or the 3D view. Most stations are Level 2 (blue), with two to six ports; only two have DC fast charging (green). Click a station for its ports, network, connectors and the date it was last confirmed. The Taxi stands and EV charging layer shows the chargers volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap, which can differ.
caveats: Only public stations reported to the Data Center are listed; chargers at homes, workplaces and many businesses are not.
A station can close or change between confirmations; the pop-up gives the date.
layers.evcharge.source_detail: NTAD Alternative Fueling Stations (layer 0): id, station_name, city, latitude, longitude, status_code, access_code, ev_network, ev_dc_fast_num, ev_level2_evse_num, ev_level1_evse_num, ev_connector_types, date_last_confirmed, updated_at

exposure.hu_transit.plain: How many housing units are a quarter mile (400 m) or less from a transit stop, by kind of stop, counted for each municipio, barrio and census tract.
exposure.hu_transit.plain_es: Cuántas unidades de vivienda están a un cuarto de milla (400 m) o menos de una parada de transporte colectivo, por tipo de parada, en cada municipio, barrio y sector censal.
exposure.hu_transit.definition: Six fields hold the count for each area. stop_any: within 400 m of any mapped stop, station or terminal, including stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap and stops whose timetable has expired. stop_sched: within 400 m of a stop with a timetable on file (expired timetables included). stop_cur: within 400 m of a stop whose operator's timetable has not ended on the as_of date of the file. stop_freq: within 400 m of a current stop with 20 or more weekday departures. stop_sat and stop_sun: within 400 m of a current stop with Saturday or Sunday service. Each set lies inside the one before it: a frequent stop is a current stop, a current stop is a scheduled stop, a scheduled stop is a stop. Since 2026-10-16 two more fields measure by walking along mapped roads (walknet.py, site/data/roads.bin): walk_cur, within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable, and walk_freq, within a 400 m walk of a frequent stop. walk_cur lies inside stop_cur and walk_freq inside both walk_cur and stop_freq. A block with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its straight-line test. Island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot: walk_cur 403,421 residents (12.3%) against stop_cur 729,507 (22.2%).
exposure.hu_transit.method: exposure.py counts each 2020 Census block whole, by its internal point (the Census Bureau's point that always lies inside the block): inside the polygons of a layer, or within 400 m of a stop. It adds the block's 2020 housing units up to the municipio, the barrio and the census tract that hold it, so the three files agree and counts add up exactly between levels. It writes nothing unless every area's total equals the crosswalk's and every set lies inside its superset (the area flooded at 2 ft is inside the area flooded at 3 ft; a stop with a current timetable is a stop). Distances are straight lines measured as access.py measures them for tourism places and the Transit tab for residents. The block points are the Census Bureau's internal points rounded to 4 decimals (about 11 m), as the Transit tab's coverage uses them, so stop_cur equals the Transit tab's residents near a stop with a current timetable in every municipio (to the one decimal its percentage shows). exposure.py --transit recomputes these six fields every night with the transit feeds; the other families change only with a full build.
exposure.hu_transit.how_to_read: Compare areas by share: divide a count by the area's total (the total field), which puts a small barrio and a large municipio on one scale. To get a share for a group of areas (the island, a region), add the counts and the totals first, then divide; do not average the shares. It is a measure of schedule access: where a stop is within a short walk, and whether a timetable covers today.
caveats: Schedule-based, and straight-line except walk_cur and walk_freq: it does not know real-time service, hours, fares, stairs, traffic or whether the walk is safe, and públicos, taxis and ride-hailing are in no timetable. The walking fields follow mapped roads only (no footpaths); see municipalities.pop_walk_active_pct for how much the joining of blocks to roads moves them.
An expired timetable means the timetable on file no longer covers today, not that service has stopped. A stop with no feed (OpenStreetMap) has no timetable at all.

stop_sat and stop_sun are low mostly because few feeds list weekend trips: on 2026-10-06, 3 of the 18 operators whose timetable had not ended (ATI, Guaynabo and Vega Alta) list Saturday departures and 1 (ATI) lists Sunday departures. A low count does not show that there is no weekend service.

stop_sched can differ from the Transit tab's residents near a scheduled stop (municipalities.json, pop_served_400m) by up to 0.5% of a municipio's residents (287 residents in Vega Baja; 0.02% on the island): the Transit tab measures to the stop nearest in degrees and drops the fraction of a metre, and this series measures to every stop in metres.
A census block is counted whole by one point, so a block that a boundary cuts is counted in or out by its internal point: near an edge the count can be higher or lower than the true number.
A housing unit is a house, an apartment, a mobile home or a room meant as separate living quarters; people in group quarters (a dormitory, a nursing home) are not in housing units.
exposure.hu_transit.geography: 78 municipios, 901 barrios and 981 census tracts, in three files
exposure.hu_transit.source_detail: 2020 Census blocks (TIGERweb layer 10); stops in transport.json; timetable end dates in operators.json

climb.walk_steep_res.plain: About how many people live within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable but have a stretch on the way steeper than a wheelchair ramp may be.
climb.walk_steep_res.plain_es: Cuántas personas, aproximadamente, viven a 400 m o menos a pie de una parada con horario vigente pero tienen en el camino un tramo más empinado de lo que puede ser una rampa para silla de ruedas.
climb.walk_steep_res.definition: The residents within a 400 m walk of a current stop whose walk has a 30 m stretch rising or falling more than 1 in 12 (8.33%), the steepest running slope of a ramp under the 2010 ADA Standards. A count; an estimate.
climb.walk_steep_res.method: climb.py takes the 2020 census blocks within a 400 m walk along mapped roads of a stop with a current timetable on 2026-10-29 (the rule of access.py: 4,914 blocks, 405,841 residents, the same as the published 'within a 400 m walk'), traces each block's shortest walk to its nearest current stop (walknet.nearest_paths) and reads the ground's height every 10 m along the roads (USGS 3DEP, interpolated between the four nearest cells), from the road nearest the block to the stop. The round-trip climb is the sum of the rises and falls; a walk is steep when a 30 m stretch rises or falls more than 1 in 12. 99 walks whose block or stop is on no walkable road are read along the straight line, as access.py measures them. A block counts whole in the barrio the crosswalk gives it; the median is weighted by residents. Checks at every build: the residents add up to the published walkers; Puerto Rico's median between 0 and 30 m; Barranquitas, Jayuya and Orocovis above it; Cataño and Toa Baja below it.
climb.walk_steep_res.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 55,648 residents. Most: San Juan (12,793), Guaynabo (11,726), Bayamón (5,414).
caveats: Only the residents within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable are counted: in most municipios few or none are, so most areas have no value.
Heights are of the bare ground at about 10 m: a road on a bridge or an embankment reads the valley or the slope below, and a short steep stretch can be smoothed out.
Mapped roads only: steps, sidewalks and footpaths are not on the map, and a block's walk starts at the road nearest its point, not at a door.
Where few residents live within a walk, one block moves the figure a lot.
climb.walk_steep_res.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; also 901 barrios (values only where residents live within a 400 m walk of a current stop)
climb.walk_steep_res.source_detail: USGS 3D Elevation Program, 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) seamless DEM, tiles USGS_13_n18w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n18w068_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w066_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w067_20260722.tif, USGS_13_n19w068_20260722.tif; walks along mapped roads (roads.bin) to the stops with a current timetable on 2026-10-29 (transport.json, operators.json); 2020 census blocks.
