municipalities.muni_system.plain: Whether the municipality runs its own bus or trolley system that reports to the federal transit database, and whether its public timetable is still valid. Empty when no such system is listed.
municipalities.muni_system.plain_es: Si el municipio opera su propio sistema de guaguas o trolleys que informa a la base de datos federal de transporte colectivo, y si su horario público sigue vigente. Queda vacío cuando no aparece ningún sistema así.
municipalities.muni_system.definition: Status of the public timetable (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, feed) of the municipal transit system that the National Transit Database (NTD) checklist lists for this municipality. The status comes from the feed's end date compared with the build date of the transit data (2026-10-02 in the current data): current when the end date is more than 60 days away, expired when it is earlier than the build date, none when the system is on the checklist but no public feed was found. The field is empty (null) when the observatory matched no municipal system from the checklist. The code also defines expiring (ends within 60 days), unknown (no end date) and broken (the feed could not be read).
municipalities.muni_system.method: network.py reads the list of Puerto Rico agencies in the National Transit Database of the Federal Transit Administration (through the Transitland Atlas copy of the 2023 table), keeps the agencies named for a municipality, and looks for a public GTFS feed of each in the registry of the National RTAP (Rural Transit Assistance Program) portal. For each feed it takes the latest end date among the service calendars and sets the status. build.py copies the status of the municipality's system into this field.
municipalities.muni_system.how_to_read: Current means a valid timetable is published. It does not mean buses run on time. Empty does not mean the municipality has no bus service: the checklist may not list its system. None means the observatory found no feed in the National RTAP registry; the municipality may publish a timetable elsewhere. The checklist is the federal 2023 reporting year, so a system that began or stopped later may be missing or listed in error. Current is judged on the latest end date of any service calendar in the feed, so it shows that some service is dated ahead, not that every route is valid. The Municipality tab shows current as "schedule published", expired as "schedule expired" and none as "no public schedule". In the 2026-10 snapshot, 14 municipalities show current, 7 expired, 15 none and 42 are empty; expiring, unknown and broken do not occur.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Cabo Rojo, Canóvanas and Corozal publish timetable feeds that the observatory reads (their stops count in gtfs_stops and pop_served_muni), but the observatory matches no NTD agency to them, so this field is empty and muni_system_routes is 0 for them.
The value is fixed at the build or nightly refresh. The Transit tab recomputes each feed's state from its end date whenever the page opens, so it can show expired where this field still says current.
Only one system is recorded per municipality.

values.current: A timetable is published and its end date is more than 60 days after the build date.
values.expired: A timetable is published but its end date is before the build date, so its dates have run out.
values.none: The municipality's system is on the NTD checklist but no public timetable feed was found.
values.(empty): The observatory matched no municipal system to this municipality from the NTD checklist. Some municipalities whose feeds the observatory reads are in this group (see the caveats).

municipalities.muni_system.source_detail: FTA (Federal Transit Administration) NTD agency list via Transitland Atlas (2023 GTFS weblinks table); National RTAP (Rural Transit Assistance Program) portal registry

view.label: Map, Municipality tab: Municipal system chip

municipalities.muni_system_routes.plain: How many routes the municipality's own transit system lists in its public timetable feed. It is 0 when the municipality has no such feed.
municipalities.muni_system_routes.plain_es: Cuántas rutas incluye el sistema de transporte colectivo propio del municipio en su fuente pública de horarios. Es 0 cuando el municipio no tiene esa fuente.
municipalities.muni_system_routes.definition: Number of routes in the feed of the municipal system matched to this municipality (see muni_system) that the observatory can draw on the map: each has a route shape in the feed, or a trip that visits at least two stops at different places. Routes with neither are skipped. The count covers the whole feed, including routes that leave the municipality. It is 0 when muni_system is empty or none.
municipalities.muni_system_routes.method: network.py reads the routes of each feed and keeps those it can draw. build.py copies the count of the municipality's system, or 0 when no system is matched.
municipalities.muni_system_routes.how_to_read: A higher number means more routes in the timetable. It does not measure trips, frequency or coverage. A feed whose timetable has expired still counts. In the 2026-10 snapshot the largest value is 11 (Guaynabo).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, a municipality with a feed that is not matched to it (Cabo Rojo, Canóvanas, Corozal) shows 0 although its feed has routes.
Routes of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed are not counted here.
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it.
municipalities.muni_system_routes.source_detail: Municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) feeds (National RTAP, Rural Transit Assistance Program, portal); NTD (National Transit Database) agency list

transit.operator_discovery.plain: The observatory starts from the federal list of transit agencies that report to the National Transit Database, then looks for each agency's public timetable feed. In the 2026-10 snapshot it lists 44 operators and says which ones publish a feed.
transit.operator_discovery.plain_es: El observatorio parte de la lista federal de agencias de transporte colectivo que informan a la National Transit Database (base de datos nacional de transporte colectivo) y luego busca la fuente pública de horarios de cada agencia. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 hay 44 operadores en la lista, y dice cuáles publican una fuente de horarios.
transit.operator_discovery.definition: 1. Checklist: the 2023 table of General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) web links of the National Transit Database (NTD, run by the Federal Transit Administration), read through the Transitland Atlas copy on GitHub. An agency is kept when its name matches a municipality (a municipal operator), contains Metropolitan Bus Authority (AMA), Highway and Transportation Authority or Público (públicos), or Maritime Transport (the ferry authority). Other agencies are skipped, and a City of San Juan in Texas is skipped by its NTD id. 2. Feeds: the Atlas registry of the National Rural Transit Assistance Program (RTAP) portal is read for municipal static GTFS feed URLs; the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed comes from its open data page. 3. Volunteer routes: OpenStreetMap routes are added as a separate operator. 4. An operator on the checklist with no feed gets status none (or in_ati for AMA and the ferry authority, whose services are in the ATI feed).
transit.operator_discovery.method: network.discover reads both lists whenever a refresh is requested (the nightly refresh always requests one) and otherwise uses its saved copy; if the lists cannot be reached it falls back to the saved copy. A municipality that uploads a feed to the registry appears at the next refresh.
transit.operator_discovery.how_to_read: The list is the federal checklist plus ATI, the feeds found and the OpenStreetMap routes. It is not a census of every vehicle service on the island.
caveats: A private público or a bus service that neither reports to the NTD nor publishes a feed is not listed.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, Cabo Rojo, Canóvanas and Corozal publish feeds but are not on the NTD checklist, so their records have a null municipality and a null ntd_id. For these three, the municipality fields muni_system and muni_system_routes in municipalities.json therefore read null and 0, even though they publish feeds.
The checklist is the report-year 2023 table, so agencies that started or stopped reporting later are not reflected.
transit.operator_discovery.source_detail: FTA National Transit Database 2023 GTFS weblinks table (2023-gtfs-weblinks.csv, report year 2023), read through the Transitland Atlas copy on GitHub; Transitland Atlas registry file feeds/nationalrtap.org.dmfr.json for the National RTAP portal feeds; ATI file PRITA_GTFS.zip

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

measures.operators_by_status.plain: How many transit operators publish a schedule, and whether it is current, about to expire or expired. On 2026-10-02, 25 operators publish a schedule and 16 publish none. The other 3 are two that run inside the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and one group of routes mapped by volunteers.
measures.operators_by_status.plain_es: Cuántos operadores de transporte colectivo publican un horario, y si está vigente, por vencer o vencido. El 2026-10-02, 25 operadores publican un horario y 16 no publican ninguno. Los otros 3 son dos que operan dentro de la fuente de horarios de la Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) y un grupo de rutas mapeadas por personas voluntarias.
measures.operators_by_status.definition: The operators listed are Puerto Rico agencies in the federal National Transit Database (municipal systems, the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA, the Metropolitan Bus Authority), the Puerto Rico Highway and Transportation Authority (públicos) and the Puerto Rico Maritime Transport Authority (ferries)), ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado), and one group for routes that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. An operator with a feed has a status from the end date of its feed compared with today's date in Puerto Rico. The others have a fixed status ('No public feed', 'In the ATI feed' or 'Community-mapped'). 'Publish a schedule' means the status is current, expiring or expired.
measures.operators_by_status.method: network.py reads each operator's feed and takes the last service date in its calendar (or the feed's own end date when there is no calendar). site/js/network.js (opStatus) compares it with today's date in Puerto Rico: expired when the date has passed, expiring when 60 days or fewer remain, current otherwise.
measures.operators_by_status.how_to_read: As of the build on 2026-10-02 the tab said 'operators publish a schedule (17 current, 1 expiring, 7 expired)'. The tab recalculates the split from today's date in Puerto Rico, so it changes as feeds pass their end date. A current status means the timetable's dates cover today, not that service runs as planned. The file of 2026-10-02 lists 44 operators.
caveats: Expiry is judged from one date in the feed. A feed can be out of date in practice while its end date is still ahead.
An operator with no feed may still run service. 'No public feed' says no timetable data were found, not that there is no service.
The operators come from the federal National Transit Database checklist, ATI's feed and OpenStreetMap. An operator in none of them is not listed.

values.current: On 2026-10-02: 17 operators. The last service date is more than 60 days away ('Current').
values.expiring: On 2026-10-02: 1 operator. The last service date is today or up to 60 days away ('Expires soon').
values.expired: On 2026-10-02: 7 operators. The last service date has passed ('Expired').
values.none: On 2026-10-02: 16 operators. They report to the National Transit Database but no public timetable feed was found ('No public feed').
values.in_ati: On 2026-10-02: 2 operators. The AMA buses and the Maritime Transport Authority ferries run inside the ATI feed ('In the ATI feed').
values.community: On 2026-10-02: 1 group. Routes that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap; no timetable ('Community-mapped').
values.broken: On 2026-10-02: 0 operators. A feed was found but could not be read ('Feed error').
values.unknown: On 2026-10-02: 0 operators. A feed was read but has no end date ('Dates unknown').

measures.operators_by_status.source_detail: operators.json (feed.status, feed.end); network.py (feed_status, discover); site/js/network.js (opStatus, renderNetSummary)

view.label: Map, Transit tab: summary figures and Operators list

transit.operators_file.plain: One file with the list of operators and the state of their timetables, a check of real-time data, residents near stops in each municipality, and places where stops of two systems are close.
transit.operators_file.plain_es: Un archivo con la lista de operadores y el estado de sus horarios, una revisión de los datos en tiempo real, los residentes cerca de paradas en cada municipio y los lugares donde hay paradas de dos sistemas cerca una de otra.
transit.operators_file.definition: The file operators.json is one JSON object with six keys, listed under Codes. A feed is the set of files, in the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format, in which one operator publishes its stops, routes, trips and times. The parts of the file have their own entries: the operator record, real-time data, residents counted for coverage and integration points.
transit.operators_file.method: Written by network.py and build.py, and rewritten every night by refresh_network.py. Operators with no feed (status none) come last; among the others the regional operator, Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), comes first and the rest follow by short name.
transit.operators_file.how_to_read: Start with the operator record for the state of each feed, then the coverage records for residents near stops.
caveats: The status stored in the file is the one worked out on the build date. The map recomputes it from the feed end date each time the page opens.
The files do not record when each feed was last downloaded. If a download fails, the previous copy of that feed is kept, so the build date does not prove that every feed was refreshed that night.

Terms differ by source. The terms of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) say the data are provided as is, without warranty, and that an app built on them must make clear it is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI. The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. Parts drawn from OpenStreetMap are under the Open Database License (credit and share-alike). Check each source's terms before reuse.
An operator record can have feed.url set to null when its feed address is not a public web page, and an operator with no feed may have no address at all (see Transit operator record).

values.built: The build date (2026-10-02 in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.operators: A list of operator records (see Transit operator record): 44 in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.live: An object with checked (the date real-time sources were checked: 2026-10-02 in the 2026-10 snapshot) and sources (a list of checks, 6 in the 2026-10 snapshot; see Real-time vehicle data).
values.coverage: An object with one record for each of the 78 municipalities, keyed by municipality name (for example Vega Baja). Each record holds the residents counted and the residents within 400 m of scheduled stops (see Residents counted for coverage).
values.transfers: A list of pairs of nearby stops of different operators (366 in the 2026-10 snapshot; see Integration points).
values.transfers_total: The number of pairs found before the list is cut at 600 (366 in the 2026-10 snapshot, so all are present).

transit.operators_file.source_detail: FTA National Transit Database 2023 GTFS weblinks table (2023-gtfs-weblinks.csv, report year 2023), read through the Transitland Atlas copy on GitHub; Transitland Atlas registry file feeds/nationalrtap.org.dmfr.json for the National RTAP portal feeds; ATI file PRITA_GTFS.zip

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

transit.feed_dates.plain: The first and last date covered by an operator's published timetable, the feed's version label and the agency name written inside the feed.
transit.feed_dates.plain_es: La primera y la última fecha que cubre el horario publicado de un operador, la etiqueta de versión de la fuente de horarios y el nombre de la agencia escrito dentro de ella.
transit.feed_dates.definition: A feed is the set of files, in the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format, in which one operator publishes its stops, routes, trips and times. feed.start and feed.end: the earliest start date and the latest end date among the feed's service patterns (calendar.txt); if the feed has no calendar, the dates in feed_info.txt. Written as YYYY-MM-DD. feed.version: the feed_version text (null for 2 feeds in the 2026-10 snapshot). feed.agency: the first agency name in the feed. In the build of 2026-10-02 the earliest start is 2023-01-01 and the latest end is 2029-12-31.
transit.feed_dates.method: parse_gtfs in network.py. An operator without a feed has none of these keys.
transit.feed_dates.how_to_read: feed.end is the date after which the published timetable no longer applies.
caveats: start and end come from the whole feed. A single route's own service can end earlier.
The end date is what the publisher entered. In the build of 2026-10-02, Bayamón and Jayuya end on 2029-12-31, far later than the other feeds.
The agency name is the one in the feed and can differ from the operator name (for example Sistema Integrado de Transportación del Sur for Ponce).
The files do not record when each feed was last downloaded. If a download fails, the previous copy of that feed is kept, so the build date does not prove that every feed was refreshed that night.
The feed object also holds url, the address the timetable was downloaded from. It can be null (see Transit operator record).

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

transit.feed_flags.plain: Three details about a feed: whether it has route shapes, whether it lists weekend service, and how many of its routes list stops out of order.
transit.feed_flags.plain_es: Tres detalles de una fuente de horarios: si trae la forma de las rutas, si incluye servicio de fin de semana y cuántas de sus rutas tienen las paradas fuera de orden.
transit.feed_flags.definition: feed.has_shapes: true when at least one route is drawn from a shape in the feed (6 of 25 feeds in the 2026-10 snapshot). feed.weekend_service: true when any route has Saturday or Sunday trips; in the 2026-10 snapshot this holds for 4 feeds: Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), Guaynabo, Juncos and Vega Alta. feed.order_issue: the number of the operator's routes with an out-of-order stop list; the key exists only when it is above 0 (in the 2026-10 snapshot, Patillas, 5).
transit.feed_flags.method: parse_gtfs and build_network in network.py. The OpenStreetMap (OSM) operator has has_shapes true and no weekend_service.
transit.feed_flags.how_to_read: has_shapes false means the operator's lines on the map are drawn along roads by the observatory.
caveats: weekend_service false means the feed lists no Saturday or Sunday trips. Service may exist without being published.

values.true: The condition holds for the feed.
values.false: The condition does not hold, or the feed does not say.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

transit.feed_status.plain: Says whether an operator's published timetable is still in force: current (more than 60 days left), expiring (60 days or fewer) or expired (the end date has passed). It does not say whether the service runs.
transit.feed_status.plain_es: Dice si el horario publicado de un operador sigue vigente: vigente (le quedan más de 60 días), por vencer (60 días o menos) o vencido (la fecha final ya pasó). No dice si el servicio opera.
transit.feed_status.definition: The state of an operator's public timetable, worked out from the feed's end date (feed.end). Expired: the end date is before today. Expiring: the end date is today or up to 60 days ahead. Current: the end date is more than 60 days ahead. Other values apply to operators without a feed or with special cases (for example in_ati: the operator's services are inside the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, ATI). The stored status uses the build date; the map recomputes it from the Puerto Rico calendar date each time the page opens, so a page opened later never shows current for a feed that has ended.
transit.feed_status.method: feed_status in network.py (build time) and opStatus in network.js (page open). Text on the map: Current, Expires soon, Expired, No public feed, In the ATI feed, Community-mapped.
transit.feed_status.how_to_read: Use current for planning only after checking the end date. Treat expired timetables as history.
caveats: Expired means the published file ended. The operator may still run service; the public file may simply not have been updated.
Current means the published timetable has not ended. It does not mean vehicles run on time or at all.
The code broken (the feed could not be read; map label Feed error) and unknown (no end date; map label Dates unknown) exist in the program but are not present in the 2026-10 snapshot.

Stops and routes of expired operators stay in the other files. Their lines and stops look the same as current ones on the map; the Expired badge appears only when a route is opened and in the Operators list, and a stop's popup gives the end date of its timetable. The observatory leaves them out of the vehicles-on-their-timetable layer, out of the active coverage figures and out of the access fields of tourism places that need a current timetable.
The feed object also holds url, the address the timetable was downloaded from. It can be null (see Transit operator record).

values.current: The feed's end date is more than 60 days away. 17 operators on 2026-10-02.
values.expiring: The feed ends within 60 days (map label: Expires soon). 1 operator on 2026-10-02.
values.expired: The feed's end date has passed. 7 operators on 2026-10-02.
values.none: The operator is on the federal checklist, but no timetable feed was found in the registry the observatory reads. It may publish elsewhere. 16 operators on 2026-10-02.
values.in_ati: The operator's services are inside the ATI feed (the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses, AMA, and the Maritime Transport Authority ferries). 2 operators on 2026-10-02.
values.community: Routes mapped by volunteers in OpenStreetMap; there is no timetable. 1 operator on 2026-10-02.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

transit.operator_record.plain: One record per operator: its name, type, how many routes, stops and weekday trips it has, and the state of its public timetable feed.
transit.operator_record.plain_es: Un registro por operador: su nombre, su tipo, cuántas rutas, paradas y viajes de lunes a viernes tiene y el estado de su fuente pública de horarios.
transit.operator_record.definition: Each record in the operators list describes one operator (44 records in the 2026-10 snapshot). Its keys are listed under Codes. For an operator with no feed, routes, stops and trips_weekday are 0 and modes is an empty list.
transit.operator_record.how_to_read: Filter on feed.status to see who has current data. Use routes, stops and trips_weekday to compare the size of systems.
caveats: feed.url is the address the timetable file was downloaded from: the ATI file, or a file uploaded to the National Rural Transit Assistance Program (RTAP) portal. It can be null: the observatory leaves it blank when the address is not a public web page.

feed.url is also null for an operator with no feed of its own when the federal list gives no link; where the list gives one, the observatory copies it without checking it. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1 of the 18 operators without a feed of their own has a link (a web page, not a timetable file) and the other 17 are null. For the OpenStreetMap routes the url is the OpenStreetMap home page, not a timetable.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 5 operators have no ntd_id: ATI, the OpenStreetMap routes and three municipal operators that are not on the federal list.
Operator-level trips_weekday counts trips with at least two stop times; the route-level count counts all trips of the route. They are equal in the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.id: Operator id: ati, osm, or a lower-case slug of the municipality or agency name (for example san_juan).
values.name: Full name of the operator.
values.short: Short name for display: ATI for the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, AMA for the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses, OpenStreetMap for the volunteer routes, the municipality's name (for example Bayamón) for a municipal operator, and the full name when no municipality is known (for example Municipality of Cabo Rojo).
values.type: Kind of operator: regional, municipal, ama, ferry, publico or community (see Operator type).
values.municipality: Municipality of a municipal operator on the federal list, else null (in the 2026-10 snapshot also null for the 3 municipal operators that are not on that list).
values.ntd_id: National Transit Database id (a number), or null (5 operators in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.modes: List of the modes of the routes it publishes (an empty list for operators with no routes).
values.trips_weekday: Weekday trips that have at least two stop times.
values.feed: Object with status, url (the address the timetable was downloaded from; it can be null, see Cautions) and, for operators with a feed, agency, version, start, end, has_shapes, weekend_service and sometimes order_issue (see the feed entries).

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

transit.operator_type.plain: Says what kind of operator a record is. There are six kinds: regional (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, ATI), municipal, bus authority (Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses, AMA), ferry, público and community (OpenStreetMap volunteers).
transit.operator_type.plain_es: Dice qué tipo de operador es un registro. Hay seis tipos: regional (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, ATI), municipal, autoridad de guaguas (Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses, AMA), lanchas, públicos y comunitario (personas voluntarias de OpenStreetMap).
transit.operator_type.definition: A code for the type of operator, set from its name on the federal checklist or fixed by the observatory (ATI is regional, OpenStreetMap is community). A feed operator that is not on the checklist is recorded as municipal.
caveats: The type says how the operator is listed, not who drives the vehicles.

values.municipal: A municipal agency. In the 2026-10 snapshot there are 39: 36 appear on the federal transit list, and 3 (Cabo Rojo, Canóvanas and Corozal) are known only because they publish a timetable feed; 24 of the 39 have a feed. The observatory does not record whether a municipality runs fixed routes or on-demand service.
values.regional: Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), the regional authority (Tren Urbano, Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA) and Metrobús buses, ferries).
values.ama: The Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA), the Metropolitan Bus Authority. Its buses are in the ATI feed, so it has no feed of its own.
values.ferry: Puerto Rico Maritime Transport Authority. Its ferries are in the ATI feed.
values.publico: Puerto Rico Highway and Transportation Authority, Público: the públicos (shared cars and vans). It publishes no timetable feed.

transit.operator_type.source_detail: FTA National Transit Database 2023 GTFS weblinks table (2023-gtfs-weblinks.csv, report year 2023), read through the Transitland Atlas copy on GitHub; Transitland Atlas registry file feeds/nationalrtap.org.dmfr.json; ATI file PRITA_GTFS.zip

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Operators list

layers.fpr_routes.plain: Municipal bus and trolley routes FPR traced in the Eastern Region where the observatory has no route yet.
layers.fpr_routes.plain_es: Las rutas municipales de guaguas y trolleys que FPR trazó en la Región Este donde el observatorio aún no tiene ruta.
layers.fpr_routes.definition: fpr_routes.geojson: one line per traced stretch the Transit routes layer does not already show, with its municipio, length in km and the share within 75 m of an observatory route. 38 stretches, 151.6 km, in 7 municipios.
layers.fpr_routes.method: FPR traced the routes in ArcGIS Pro (Municipalroutes_ExportFeatures). fpr_baseline.py measures, in metres (Puerto Rico State Plane), how much of each stretch lies within 75 m of a route in transit_routes.geojson and publishes those under half.
layers.fpr_routes.how_to_read: Switch the layer on in the Layers tab (Infrastructure and mobility: Municipal routes mapped by FPR). Click a line for its municipio and length.
caveats: A traced path, not a timetable: no stops, frequency or hours.
Most stretches have no route name; FPR can add nombre, operador and fuente in fpr_rutas_municipales.geojson.
layers.fpr_routes.geography: Lines in 7 municipios of the Eastern Region
layers.fpr_routes.source_detail: FPR Eastern Region baseline dashboard (Power BI), read 2026-10-23

view.label: Map, Layers tab: Municipal routes mapped by FPR
3D view, Layers tab: Municipal routes mapped by FPR

transit.real_time.plain: On 2 October 2026 no public real-time feed of bus, train or ferry positions was found for Puerto Rico, so the data hold no live vehicle positions. This entry lists what was checked and what each source needs.
transit.real_time.plain_es: El 2 de octubre de 2026 no se encontró ninguna fuente pública en tiempo real de las posiciones de guaguas, trenes o lanchas en Puerto Rico, así que los datos no tienen posiciones de vehículos en vivo. Esta entrada dice qué se revisó y qué necesita cada fuente.
transit.real_time.definition: The key live in operators.json holds checked (the check date, 2026-10-02) and sources (the list of checks, 6 on that date). Each check has id, name, status, detail and, when there is one, url. The checks of 2026-10-02 cover the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) real-time feed (listed by ATI as in development, with no feed address), the AMA Móvil app (AMA is the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses; positions shown in an app, no public data), ATI express buses (a third-party app says it uses positions the operator publishes; no public feed), municipal systems (none found), the AcuaExpreso ferries (an app, no public feed) and aircraft near Puerto Rico (community data in ADS-B format, Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast, that need a relay).
transit.real_time.method: The result of each check is written into LIVE_SOURCES in network.py (checked 2026-10-02). The observatory does not test the sources automatically.
transit.real_time.how_to_read: Where the observatory shows vehicles moving, it is replaying a timetable. See Vehicles on their timetable now.
caveats: The check is a snapshot. A feed published after the check date will not be known until someone updates the list.
The statuses describe public data. An operator can have private tracking that is not shared.

values.not published: The operator has announced the feed but no address exists. Example: the ATI real-time feed, which ATI lists as en desarrollo (in development).
values.app only: Positions are shown in a mobile app, and no public data feed sits behind it (AMA Móvil, the ferries).
values.private feed: A third-party app says it shows positions that the operator publishes. No public feed address exists, and access is said to require a request to ATI (the ATI express buses).
values.none found: No real-time feed exists in the public registries (municipal systems).
values.available, needs a relay: Free live data exist but their servers do not allow calls from a web page, so a small relay service is needed (aircraft, ADS-B).

transit.real_time.source_detail: operators.json key live: live.checked (2026-10-02) and live.sources (6 items with id, name, status, detail and url). Pages checked: ATI open data page, AMA Móvil (AMATrack) on Google Play, transPRte on the Apple App Store, ATI urban transportation page, community ADS-B networks

view.label: Map, Transit tab: What is live

exposure.pop_transit.plain: How many residents are a quarter mile (400 m) or less from a transit stop, by kind of stop, counted for each municipio, barrio and census tract.
exposure.pop_transit.plain_es: Cuántas personas residentes están a un cuarto de milla (400 m) o menos de una parada de transporte colectivo, por tipo de parada, en cada municipio, barrio y sector censal.
exposure.pop_transit.definition: Six fields hold the count for each area. stop_any: within 400 m of any mapped stop, station or terminal, including stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap and stops whose timetable has expired. stop_sched: within 400 m of a stop with a timetable on file (expired timetables included). stop_cur: within 400 m of a stop whose operator's timetable has not ended on the as_of date of the file. stop_freq: within 400 m of a current stop with 20 or more weekday departures. stop_sat and stop_sun: within 400 m of a current stop with Saturday or Sunday service. Each set lies inside the one before it: a frequent stop is a current stop, a current stop is a scheduled stop, a scheduled stop is a stop. Since 2026-10-16 two more fields measure by walking along mapped roads (walknet.py, site/data/roads.bin): walk_cur, within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable, and walk_freq, within a 400 m walk of a frequent stop. walk_cur lies inside stop_cur and walk_freq inside both walk_cur and stop_freq. A block with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its straight-line test. Island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot: walk_cur 403,421 residents (12.3%) against stop_cur 729,507 (22.2%).
exposure.pop_transit.method: exposure.py counts each 2020 Census block whole, by its internal point (the Census Bureau's point that always lies inside the block): inside the polygons of a layer, or within 400 m of a stop. It adds the block's 2020 residents up to the municipio, the barrio and the census tract that hold it, so the three files agree and counts add up exactly between levels. It writes nothing unless every area's total equals the crosswalk's and every set lies inside its superset (the area flooded at 2 ft is inside the area flooded at 3 ft; a stop with a current timetable is a stop). Distances are straight lines measured as access.py measures them for tourism places and the Transit tab for residents. The block points are the Census Bureau's internal points rounded to 4 decimals (about 11 m), as the Transit tab's coverage uses them, so stop_cur equals the Transit tab's residents near a stop with a current timetable in every municipio (to the one decimal its percentage shows). exposure.py --transit recomputes these six fields every night with the transit feeds; the other families change only with a full build.
exposure.pop_transit.how_to_read: Compare areas by share: divide a count by the area's total (the total field), which puts a small barrio and a large municipio on one scale. To get a share for a group of areas (the island, a region), add the counts and the totals first, then divide; do not average the shares. It is a measure of schedule access: where a stop is within a short walk, and whether a timetable covers today.
caveats: Schedule-based, and straight-line except walk_cur and walk_freq: it does not know real-time service, hours, fares, stairs, traffic or whether the walk is safe, and públicos, taxis and ride-hailing are in no timetable. The walking fields follow mapped roads only (no footpaths); see municipalities.pop_walk_active_pct for how much the joining of blocks to roads moves them.
An expired timetable means the timetable on file no longer covers today, not that service has stopped. A stop with no feed (OpenStreetMap) has no timetable at all.

stop_sat and stop_sun are low mostly because few feeds list weekend trips: on 2026-10-06, 3 of the 18 operators whose timetable had not ended (ATI, Guaynabo and Vega Alta) list Saturday departures and 1 (ATI) lists Sunday departures. A low count does not show that there is no weekend service.

stop_sched can differ from the Transit tab's residents near a scheduled stop (municipalities.json, pop_served_400m) by up to 0.5% of a municipio's residents (287 residents in Vega Baja; 0.02% on the island): the Transit tab measures to the stop nearest in degrees and drops the fraction of a metre, and this series measures to every stop in metres.
A census block is counted whole by one point, so a block that a boundary cuts is counted in or out by its internal point: near an edge the count can be higher or lower than the true number.
exposure.pop_transit.geography: 78 municipios, 901 barrios and 981 census tracts, in three files
exposure.pop_transit.source_detail: 2020 Census blocks (TIGERweb layer 10); stops in transport.json; timetable end dates in operators.json

municipalities.uber_listed.plain: Whether Uber's own Puerto Rico cities page names the municipality, as Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) recorded it on 2026-10-01. It is a yes/no listing, not coverage: it does not show that a driver is nearby.
municipalities.uber_listed.plain_es: Si la página de ciudades de Puerto Rico del propio Uber nombra el municipio, según lo registró Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) el 2026-10-01. Es un listado de sí o no, no de cobertura: no indica que haya una persona conductora cerca.
municipalities.uber_listed.definition: True when the municipality's name appears in the list of Puerto Rico cities on Uber's cities page on the date FPR checked it, 2026-10-01; false when it does not. The list is stored in transport.py; the observatory does not read Uber's page by itself.
municipalities.uber_listed.method: The list is fixed in the code: transport.py holds the municipality names Uber showed on its Puerto Rico cities page and the check date (UBER_CHECKED). A municipality is true when its name is in the list.
municipalities.uber_listed.how_to_read: True means only that Uber names the municipality. It does not measure the area served, wait times, price or whether drivers are available. The observatory holds no Uber coverage area or driver data. False means the municipality was not named on that page, not that service is impossible.
caveats: One page on one date. Uber can change its list without notice, and the observatory does not update it between builds. It was not re-checked after 2026-10-01.
Uber's page says its service reaches beyond the places it lists, so a municipality that is not listed may still have Uber service.
The source is a company's public web page, and the observatory records only a yes/no per municipality. Check Uber's terms before reusing the list.
The map shades listed municipalities in one colour and the others in grey; the legend repeats that this is a listing, not measured coverage.

values.true: Listed: the municipality's name was on Uber's Puerto Rico cities page when checked on 2026-10-01 (57 municipalities).
values.false: Not listed: the name was not on that page on 2026-10-01 (21 municipalities: Adjuntas, Aibonito, Barranquitas, Ciales, Comerío, Culebra, Florida, Jayuya, Las Marías, Maricao, Maunabo, Moca, Morovis, Naranjito, Orocovis, Patillas, Sabana Grande, San Sebastián, Utuado, Vieques, Villalba).

roads.transit_snapping.plain: Some transit feeds give no route shape, so the build joins consecutive stops along the road network. The line then follows streets and does not cut across blocks.
roads.transit_snapping.plain_es: Algunas fuentes de horarios no traen la forma de la ruta, así que la compilación une las paradas seguidas por la red de carreteras. Así la línea sigue las calles y no corta a través de las manzanas.
roads.transit_snapping.definition: Each published route line carries a geometry source. A route with a shape in the feed keeps it ('shape'). A route without one is drawn along roads between its stops ('roads'; 'roads_inferred' when the feed lists the stops out of order). It is joined by straight lines between stops ('stops') when too few pairs of stops can be snapped (less than 60% in a direction), or when the feed lists the stops out of order and the route has more than 45 distinct stops. Routes that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap keep their own lines ('osm').
roads.transit_snapping.method: For each pair of consecutive stops: closer than 25 m, keep a two-point line. Otherwise snap both stops to roads within 500 m and find the fastest road path. Accept it when its length is at most 3 times the straight-line distance plus 400 m; if not, that pair stays a straight line. A route counts as road-following when at least 60% of the pairs in each direction snap. When the feed's stop order is not geographic (the path through the stops in listed order is more than 2.5 times longer than a nearest-neighbour tour, or the stops are in alphabetical order), the order of visit is inferred from road travel distances for routes with up to 45 distinct stops. The final line is simplified to about 3 m (0.00003 degree).
roads.transit_snapping.how_to_read: A line on the map that follows streets is an estimate of where the vehicle drives. The exact street may differ from the one drawn. For the number of routes drawn each way in the current snapshot, see the entry on how the route line was drawn.
caveats: The line is an approximate path between stops. The exact street may differ.
Where a feed lists the stops out of order, the order of visit is inferred and the route's times are not used in the timetable replay.
The geometry_source field of the routes file records which of these methods drew each route.

values.shape: Line from the operator's own route shape.
values.roads: The feed has no route shape; the line follows roads between the stops in listed order.
values.roads_inferred: The feed lists the stops out of travel order; the order of visit is inferred and the line follows roads.
values.osm: Line mapped by volunteers in OpenStreetMap.
values.stops: Too few pairs of stops could be snapped to roads, or the stops are out of order and the route has more than 45 distinct stops; straight lines join the stops.

roads.transit_snapping.geography: Routes of every operator in the observatory
roads.transit_snapping.source_detail: network.py (snap_routes, RoadSnapper, order_quality) with roads.bin; GTFS means General Transit Feed Specification, the standard format of public timetable feeds

roads.router.plain: The planner snaps each point you choose to the nearest road within 500 m, then finds the fastest road path between the points at planning speeds. A leg with no road path is drawn as a straight line.
roads.router.plain_es: El planificador lleva cada punto que se escoge a la carretera más cercana, dentro de 500 m, y luego busca el camino más rápido por carretera entre los puntos, a las velocidades de planificación. Un tramo sin camino por carretera se dibuja como una línea recta.
roads.router.definition: Fastest path on the road graph, where each road piece costs its length divided by the planning speed of its class. Two-way pieces can be used in both directions; one-way pieces only from start to end. The same method runs in the browser (roads.js, for the route planner) and at build time (roads.py, for drawing published transit routes).
roads.router.method: Snap: each chosen point goes to the nearest point on any road piece within 500 m, by straight-line distance. Search: an A* search (a shortest-path search guided by straight-line distance) finds the fastest path between consecutive points, starting and finishing anywhere along a road piece. Check: a leg counts as 'on roads' only when both points snap and the road path is no longer than 4 times the straight-line distance plus 1,500 m. Otherwise the leg is drawn straight and marked as unable to follow roads.
roads.router.how_to_read: The drawn line is one plausible road path. A real bus may take another street.
caveats: Snapping uses straight-line distance. A point can be matched to a road on the other side of a river or a fence.
The router has no turn costs, signals or traffic. It picks the fastest path at planning speeds, not the shortest and not the path a bus takes.
The detour limit is a plausibility test. It does not prove that no road connection exists.
A route can have at most 8 points: From, To and up to 6 added stops.

values.Snap radius: 500 m. A point farther than this from every road makes its legs straight lines.
values.Detour limit: A road path longer than 4 times the straight-line distance plus 1,500 m is rejected, and the leg is drawn straight.
values.Gap between a point and its road: The straight-line distance is added to the leg length and counted at walking pace, 1.4 m/s (5 km/h).
values.Leg that cannot follow roads: Drawn straight, length is the straight-line distance, time counted at 8 m/s (28.8 km/h).
values.Planning speeds: 12 to 90 km/h by road class; see the entry on road classes.

roads.router.geography: Main island of Puerto Rico, Vieques and Culebra (separate pieces of the graph). Mona Island has no roads in the file
roads.router.source_detail: site/js/roads.js (snap, route, path) and roads.py (Roads); parameters used by site/js/plan.js

roads.class.plain: Every road piece has a class code from 0 to 14, taken from OpenStreetMap, and each class has a planning speed. The router uses the speeds to pick the fastest road and to estimate time.
roads.class.plain_es: Cada tramo de carretera tiene un código de clase del 0 al 14, tomado de OpenStreetMap, y cada clase tiene una velocidad de planificación. El planificador usa esas velocidades para escoger la carretera más rápida y estimar el tiempo.
roads.class.definition: The road class is stored in the low four bits of each road piece's flag byte. The planning speed is a fixed number of kilometres per hour for each class, set in roads.py and repeated in the same order in roads.js.
roads.class.method: The class is the OpenStreetMap highway value of the road. The speeds are planning values set in the code, not measured. Only the ratios between classes decide which road is the fastest choice; the absolute values set the estimated time.
roads.class.how_to_read: Read '90' as 'the router treats this class as 90 km/h', not as a speed limit. The router picks the path with the least travel time at these speeds, so it prefers faster road classes but still avoids long detours. The class comes from OpenStreetMap. The speeds are planning values chosen by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) in the observatory's code. They are not OpenStreetMap data, so do not credit them to OpenStreetMap.
caveats: Planning speeds are not speed limits, observed speeds or bus speeds.
The class comes from volunteers' tags in OpenStreetMap. It can differ from a road's official class or its PR route number.

Kilometres add up the length of every road piece. A divided road is mapped as two one-way pieces, one for each direction, so both are counted: the motorway total is the length of both carriageways added together, not the length of the road itself. It is not lane-kilometres.
Class 13 (service) exists in the code but no road piece carries it.

roads.network.plain: A compact map of Puerto Rico's drivable roads, stored as junctions and the road pieces between them. The route planner uses it to follow streets. The file itself is not drawn on the map; transit route lines that follow streets are drawn from it.
roads.network.plain_es: Un mapa compacto de las carreteras de Puerto Rico por donde pueden pasar vehículos, guardado como intersecciones y los tramos de carretera entre ellas. El planificador de rutas lo usa para seguir las calles. El archivo no se dibuja en el mapa; de él salen las líneas de las rutas de transporte colectivo que siguen las calles.
roads.network.definition: A directed graph built from OpenStreetMap roads: junctions (including points where a long road piece was cut), road pieces (edges) and interior bend points. A divided road has one road piece for each direction, so total length counts both directions. Each road piece stores its two end junctions, its length in 2 m steps, a road class code (0 to 14), a one-way flag and the number of bend points between its ends.
roads.network.method: roads.py reads the Geofabrik Puerto Rico extract of OpenStreetMap, keeps drivable roads (see the entry on which roads are kept), cuts them into pieces at junctions, drops bend points within about 2 m of a straight line, and writes the binary file.
roads.network.how_to_read: Use it to see which streets a route can follow. It is not a full road inventory: it holds drivable roads only, as volunteers mapped them. Do not use it to measure total road length or road condition. In the 2026-10 snapshot the file holds 193,507 junctions, 226,421 road pieces and 536,209 bend points. The pieces add up to about 33,100 km, counting both directions of a divided road. The file is 6,409,964 bytes. The OpenStreetMap extract it was built from has a data timestamp of 2026-10-01 20:22 UTC (Coordinated Universal Time; Puerto Rico is 4 hours behind).
caveats: Left out: service roads (driveways, parking aisles, alleys), tracks, footpaths, cycle paths and roads tagged private, no access, no motor vehicles or no vehicles (unless tagged for buses). Some real streets are therefore absent.

A road that is missing or wrongly tagged in OpenStreetMap is missing or wrong here. The data reflect the extract of 2026-10-01. The file itself does not record that date; it was read from the extract's header.
In the 2026-10 snapshot the graph has 363 separate pieces. The largest holds 98.8% of the junctions. Vieques and Culebra are separate pieces, so a route cannot follow roads between islands.
The file has no turn bans, tolls, traffic signals, road surface, lane counts or traffic.

License: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0. Credit line: Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL). Read the terms at openstreetmap.org/copyright before reusing the data.

values.header (20 bytes): The letters PRRD, then four whole numbers: version (1), number of junctions, number of road pieces, number of bend points. All numbers are little-endian (the lowest byte comes first).
values.nodes: One pair of whole numbers per junction: x = (longitude + 68) x 100,000 and y = (latitude - 17) x 100,000. One step is 0.00001 degree, about 1.1 m.
values.edges: One 12-byte record per road piece: start junction, end junction, length in steps of 2 m (up to 65,535), a flag byte (bits 0 to 3 are the road class, bit 4 is set when the piece is one-way from start to end) and the number of bend points between its ends (0 to 250).
values.shape: The bend points of every road piece in order, each stored as a small step (dx, dy) from the previous point, in the same 0.00001 degree units.

roads.selection.plain: The road network keeps roads that cars and buses can drive. It leaves out driveways, parking aisles, footpaths and roads closed to motor vehicles.
roads.selection.plain_es: La red de carreteras incluye las vías por donde pueden pasar carros y guaguas. Deja fuera las entradas de garaje, los pasillos de estacionamientos, los caminos peatonales y las vías cerradas a vehículos de motor.
roads.selection.definition: A way in OpenStreetMap is kept when its highway tag is one of 14 values (motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, their link ramps, unclassified, residential, living_street and busway) and no access tag closes it to motor vehicles. Every other way is dropped, including highway=service.
roads.selection.method: 1. Keep ways whose highway tag is one of the 14 classes. 2. Drop a way tagged access=no or access=private, motor_vehicle=no or vehicle=no, unless it is tagged bus=yes or bus=designated. 3. Set direction: oneway=yes, true or 1 means one-way along the way; oneway=-1 or reverse means one-way against it; oneway=no means two-way. With no oneway tag, only motorways, motorway ramps and roundabouts are one-way. 4. A point becomes a junction where two or more ways meet, or where a way starts or ends. The part of a way between two junctions is a road piece. A piece that starts and ends at the same junction with no bend points is dropped. 5. Drop bend points within about 2 m of a straight line to the end of the piece. Cut a piece with more than 250 bend points into several pieces. 6. Measure each piece along its bends and store its length in 2 m steps.
roads.selection.how_to_read: Use this entry to see why a street you know cannot be used by the router. It may be a service road, a path, a road under construction or a road tagged private in OpenStreetMap.
caveats: A road tagged access=destination or access=customers is kept.
Roads tagged highway=construction or highway=proposed are not kept.
A oneway=reversible tag is not read. Such a road is treated as two-way unless it is a motorway or a roundabout.
Pedestrian streets are not in the road network. They do appear in the place-name index.
roads.selection.geography: Main island of Puerto Rico, Vieques and Culebra (separate pieces of the graph). Mona Island has no roads in the file

infrastructure.crash_fatal.plain: How many crashes in the municipio killed at least one person each year.
infrastructure.crash_fatal.plain_es: Cuántos choques en el municipio mataron por lo menos a una persona cada año.
infrastructure.crash_fatal.definition: Crashes on a public road in the municipio in which at least one person died within 30 days.
infrastructure.crash_fatal.method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
infrastructure.crash_fatal.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 275 fatal crashes in 2024. Most: San Juan (34), Bayamón (16), Caguas (10).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.
infrastructure.crash_fatal.source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).

infrastructure.crash_deaths.plain: How many people died in traffic crashes in the municipio each year.
infrastructure.crash_deaths.plain_es: Cuántas personas murieron en choques de tránsito en el municipio cada año.
infrastructure.crash_deaths.definition: People who died within 30 days of a crash on a public road in the municipio, as NHTSA's Fatality Analysis Reporting System counts them.
infrastructure.crash_deaths.method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
infrastructure.crash_deaths.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 288 deaths in 2024 (242 in 2020). Most in 2024: San Juan (35), Bayamón (16), Carolina (11).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.
infrastructure.crash_deaths.source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: People killed in traffic crashes (FARS)

infrastructure.crash_per_vkm.plain: How many people died in traffic crashes for every 100 million kilometres driven on the municipio's roads, over 2020-2024: the risk per kilometre driven.
infrastructure.crash_per_vkm.plain_es: Cuántas personas murieron en choques de tránsito por cada 100 millones de kilómetros recorridos en las carreteras del municipio, en 2020-2024: el riesgo por kilómetro recorrido.
infrastructure.crash_per_vkm.definition: The people killed in traffic crashes in the municipio over 2020-2024, divided by the vehicle-kilometres driven on its roads in those years, times 100 million. The vehicle-kilometres are those of HPMS data year 2025 (traffic_series.json), counted for each of the 5 years: a measure of risk per kilometre driven, where the rate per resident is high because much traffic passes through.
infrastructure.crash_per_vkm.method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
infrastructure.crash_per_vkm.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 1.05 over 2020-2024 (about 1.69 per 100 million vehicle-miles). Highest: Rincón (2.34), Yabucoa (2.16), Loíza (2.13); lowest: Culebra (0.00), Guayanilla (0.20), Aibonito (0.33).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.
The vehicle-kilometres are those of HPMS data year 2025, used for each of the five years; traffic changed over the period.
infrastructure.crash_per_vkm.source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: Traffic deaths per 100 million vehicle-km, 2020-2024 (FARS, HPMS)

infrastructure.crash_rate_5y.plain: How many people died in traffic crashes in the municipio each year for every 100,000 residents, averaged over 2020-2024.
infrastructure.crash_rate_5y.plain_es: Cuántas personas murieron en choques de tránsito en el municipio cada año por cada 100,000 residentes, en promedio en 2020-2024.
infrastructure.crash_rate_5y.definition: The people killed in traffic crashes in the municipio over 2020-2024, divided by the sum of its residents in those years (Census Bureau population estimates), times 100,000: a yearly rate. Five years are pooled because a municipio has few deaths a year.
infrastructure.crash_rate_5y.method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
infrastructure.crash_rate_5y.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 8.9 per 100,000 a year over 2020-2024. Highest: Santa Isabel (22.1), Guánica (21.7), Salinas (21.5); lowest: Culebra (0.0), Guayanilla (2.3), Las Marías (2.3).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.
It counts the deaths on the municipio's roads, also of people who live elsewhere: high where much traffic passes through (see the rate per vehicle-km).
infrastructure.crash_rate_5y.source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: Traffic deaths per 100,000 residents, 2020-2024 (FARS)

route_compare.busy_passes_16_19.plain: How many times, added over all its trips, the route's buses pass a high-volume intersection from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m.
route_compare.busy_passes_16_19.plain_es: Cuántas veces, sumados todos sus viajes, los autobuses de la ruta pasan por una intersección de alto volumen de 4:00 a 7:00 p.m.
route_compare.busy_passes_16_19.definition: As busy_passes_6_9, for the passes between 16:00 and 19:00 (trips leaving 16:00-19:00 for a timetable-only route).
caveats: Marked with an asterisk on the page when estimated.

route_compare.passes_estimated.plain: Whether the crossings are estimated from the number of trips, because the timetable gives times at only two stops.
route_compare.passes_estimated.plain_es: Si los cruces se estiman con el número de viajes, porque el horario da la hora en solo dos paradas.
route_compare.passes_estimated.definition: true for a timetable-only route with a route line: busy_passes_6_9 and busy_passes_16_19 are trips leaving in the period times busy_junctions.
route_compare.passes_estimated.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

route_compare.km_to_ati.plain: The straight-line distance from the route's nearest stop to the nearest ATI stop, in kilometres (0 for ATI routes).
route_compare.km_to_ati.plain_es: La distancia en línea recta de la parada más cercana de la ruta a la parada de la ATI más cercana, en kilómetros (0 en las rutas de la ATI).
route_compare.km_to_ati.definition: Minimum, over the route's stops, of the straight-line distance to the nearest ATI transit stop, in km to one decimal.
route_compare.km_to_ati.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.timetable_expired.plain: Whether the system's timetable had ended (its end date had passed) on 2026-10-19, so it may not be the service that runs today.
route_compare.timetable_expired.plain_es: Si el horario del sistema ya había terminado (su fecha final había pasado) el 2026-10-19, por lo que puede no ser el servicio que opera hoy.
route_compare.timetable_expired.definition: true when the operator's feed_end (operators table) is before as_of (2026-10-19). The page computes the flag again from feed_end and the date it is read, so a timetable that ends later is flagged from that day.
route_compare.timetable_expired.method: route_compare.py: feed_end < TODAY; route_analysis.js: feed_end < the viewer's date.
caveats: On 2026-10-19: Caguas, Fajardo, Juncos and San Lorenzo. Canóvanas's timetable ends on 2026-10-31.
route_compare.timetable_expired.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.express_two_stops.plain: Whether the route is an express with only two stops whose timed path covers the whole trip, so its speed is kept.
route_compare.express_two_stops.plain_es: Si la ruta es un expreso con solo dos paradas cuyo camino con hora cubre todo el viaje, por lo que su velocidad se conserva.
route_compare.express_two_stops.definition: true for a timetable-only route whose speed was kept (timed path at least half its route line): ATI 20, Bayamón BT-2 and BT-3, and the Caguas, Juncos and San Lorenzo routes whose two timed stops are the two ends.
route_compare.express_two_stops.method: route_compare.py: timepoints_only and speed is not blank.
caveats: The name is the script's: besides ATI 20, the routes it marks are timetable-only routes timed at both ends, not express services.
route_compare.express_two_stops.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.peak_extra_pct.plain: How much longer (or shorter, when negative) the timetable makes the trip at the morning peak than at midday.
route_compare.peak_extra_pct.plain_es: Cuánto más largo (o más corto, si es negativo) hace el horario el viaje en la hora pico de la mañana que al mediodía.
route_compare.peak_extra_pct.definition: (minutes_peak - minutes_midday) / minutes_midday x 100, to one decimal.
route_compare.peak_extra_pct.how_to_read: Zero means the operator plans no extra time for rush hour; it does not mean there is no congestion.
caveats: The operator's own plan, not observed times.
route_compare.peak_extra_pct.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.first.plain: The time the first trip of the day leaves its first stop.
route_compare.first.plain_es: La hora en que el primer viaje del día sale de su primera parada.
route_compare.first.definition: Earliest scheduled departure from the first stop among the route's weekday trips, as H:MM on a 24-hour clock.
route_compare.first.method: min of the trips' first stop times, written as H:MM.
route_compare.first.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.busy_junctions.plain: How many signalised junctions and roundabouts with an estimated 2,000 or more vehicles an hour in the design hour (one of the busiest hours of the year) lie on the route's path.
route_compare.busy_junctions.plain_es: Cuántos cruces con semáforo y rotondas con un estimado de 2,000 o más vehículos por hora en la hora de diseño (una de las horas de más tránsito del año) hay en el camino de la ruta.
route_compare.busy_junctions.definition: Signalised junctions and roundabouts (OpenStreetMap, road_features.geojson) within 20 m of the route's paths whose estimated design-hour volume (road_flow.csv: AADT x K factor of the busiest FHWA HPMS road within 30 m; K is the 30th-busiest hour of the year as a percentage of AADT, HPMS Field Manual item 26; for 48% of the junctions the observatory's class-median K) is 2,000 vehicles an hour or more. For a timetable-only route (timepoints_only: Bayamón, Caguas, Juncos and San Lorenzo, and ATI express route 20), the operator's route line in transit_routes.geojson is used instead of the timed path.
route_compare.busy_junctions.method: transit_exposure.csv (busy_junctions_on_path, written by the road-features analysis's transit_exposure.py), or a 20 m buffer of the route line for a timetable-only route.
caveats: The flow is an estimate from annual averages, not a count at the hour.
20 m can catch a junction the route passes over or under.
The flow is that of the busiest road at the junction, not necessarily the one the bus uses.
route_compare.busy_junctions.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

route_compare.busy_per_10km.plain: High-volume intersections on the path for every 10 km of route.
route_compare.busy_per_10km.plain_es: Intersecciones de alto volumen en el camino por cada 10 km de recorrido.
route_compare.busy_per_10km.definition: busy_junctions x 10 / length_km, to one decimal.
route_compare.busy_per_10km.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

route_compare.last.plain: The time the last trip of the day leaves its first stop.
route_compare.last.plain_es: La hora en que el último viaje del día sale de su primera parada.
route_compare.last.definition: Latest scheduled departure from the first stop among the route's weekday trips, as H:MM on a 24-hour clock.
route_compare.last.method: max of the trips' first stop times, written as H:MM.
route_compare.last.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.busy_passes_6_9.plain: How many times, added over all its trips, the route's buses pass a high-volume intersection from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m.
route_compare.busy_passes_6_9.plain_es: Cuántas veces, sumados todos sus viajes, los autobuses de la ruta pasan por una intersección de alto volumen de 6:00 a 9:00 a.m.
route_compare.busy_passes_6_9.definition: Each weekday trip is placed on its path by its stop times (time between two stops spread by distance), which gives the time it passes each high-volume intersection; the passes between 6:00 and 9:00 are counted. For a timetable-only route it is estimated as the trips leaving 6:00-9:00 times busy_junctions (passes_estimated).
route_compare.busy_passes_6_9.how_to_read: A measure of expected exposure to congestion, not of delay: the timetables do not say how long a bus waits at a junction.
caveats: Marked with an asterisk on the page when estimated.
route_compare.busy_passes_6_9.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.peak_headway_min.plain: Every how many minutes, on average, the route runs from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m. in its busiest direction.
route_compare.peak_headway_min.plain_es: Cada cuántos minutos, en promedio, pasa la ruta de 6:00 a 9:00 a.m. en su dirección con más viajes.
route_compare.peak_headway_min.definition: 180 minutes divided by peak_trips_one_direction, rounded to the minute. Blank when no trip leaves in that period.
route_compare.peak_headway_min.how_to_read: Planners often treat 15 minutes or less as service people can use without a timetable.
caveats: An average over three hours: two trips that leave together still count as two.
route_compare.peak_headway_min.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

route_compare.peak_trips_one_direction.plain: How many trips leave from 6:00 to 9:00 a.m. on the route's busiest stop pattern (one direction).

route_compare.peak_trips_one_direction.definition: Largest number, over the route's stop patterns, of trips whose first departure is at or after 6:00 and before 9:00.
route_compare.peak_trips_one_direction.method: route_compare.py: max of Counter(pattern of trips leaving 6:00-9:00).
route_compare.peak_trips_one_direction.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

route_compare.reaches_tren_urbano.plain_es: Si alguna parada de la ruta está a 300 m o menos de una estación del Tren Urbano.
route_compare.reaches_tren_urbano.definition: true when any stop of any of the route's patterns (or listed for the route in transport.json) is within 300 m in a straight line of a rail station.
route_compare.reaches_tren_urbano.method: route_compare.py, on the points of transport.json.

route_compare.file.plain: One row for each of 97 bus routes of the ATI and of the municipal systems of the San Juan metro area and eastern Puerto Rico, compared on five measures from their weekday timetables: service, route, peak-hour intersections, connections and nearby residents. It describes the scheduled service, not the service observed on the street.
route_compare.file.plain_es: Una fila por cada una de 97 rutas de autobús de la ATI y de los sistemas municipales del área metropolitana de San Juan y del este de Puerto Rico, comparadas en cinco medidas a partir de sus horarios de un día de semana: servicio, recorrido, intersecciones en hora pico, conexiones y residentes cercanos. Describe el servicio programado, no el servicio observado en la calle.
route_compare.file.definition: route_compare.json has two tables. routes: one record per operator and route label with a bus trip in the weekday timetable (typical Wednesday) of the ATI or of San Juan, Bayamón, Guaynabo, Caguas, Canóvanas (the metro area: a stop within 250 m of an ATI stop), Fajardo, Humacao, Juncos, San Lorenzo, Patillas or Vieques (the east), with the 30 fields of route_compare.*. operators: the 12 systems, with their name and the end date of their timetable (feed_end). The Tren Urbano is left out (its own track).
route_compare.file.method: docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/route_compare.py reads site/data (trips.json, transport.json, transit_routes.geojson, population_blocks.json) and four inputs from the road-features analysis, committed beside it: road_features.geojson (OpenStreetMap junctions and footbridges), road_flow.csv (their estimated design-hour volume from FHWA HPMS 2024: AADT x K factor), transit_exposure.csv and transit_runtime.csv (when each route's trips pass them, and its scheduled run times); make_page.py publishes the result as this file and writes the page.
route_compare.file.how_to_read: Compare routes within the same kind of timetable. A route with a full timetable (a time at every stop) is measured on its timed path; a timetable-only route (two timed stops) on the operator's line, so its length, speed and crossings are marked with an asterisk on the page.
caveats: Timetables, not observed service: delays and skipped trips are not seen.

The flow that defines a high-volume intersection is an estimate of the design-hour volume (AADT x K factor: the 30th-busiest hour of the year), not a count and not a typical weekday peak; 48% of the junctions use the observatory's class-median K, which HPMS guidance does not endorse.
Four timetables had expired on 2026-10-19 (Caguas, Fajardo, Juncos, San Lorenzo) and Canóvanas's ends on 2026-10-31.
Cataño and Toa Baja publish no GTFS timetable, so their routes are missing.
route_compare.file.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis

route_compare.length_km.plain: The length of the route's main stop pattern, in kilometres. For a timetable-only route it is the length of the line the operator draws, which can hold both directions.
route_compare.length_km.plain_es: El largo del patrón principal de paradas de la ruta, en kilómetros. En una ruta con solo horario de punto a punto es el largo de la línea que dibuja el operador, que puede incluir las dos direcciones.
route_compare.length_km.definition: Metres along the path of the stop pattern with most trips (trips.json paths), in km to one decimal. For a timetable-only route (timepoints_only: Bayamón, Caguas, Juncos and San Lorenzo, and ATI express route 20), the operator's route line in transit_routes.geojson is used instead of the timed path. Its longest part is measured, and it may draw the outbound and return trips as one line (Bayamón BR-1: 32.1 km of line, 16.0 km between its two timed stops).
route_compare.length_km.method: route_compare.py: path[-1][2] / 1000, or the route line's length for a timetable-only route.
caveats: Marked with an asterisk on the page for timetable-only routes: it is the line drawn, not one trip.
route_compare.length_km.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

route_compare.name.plain: The route's long name, usually its two ends.
route_compare.name.plain_es: El nombre largo de la ruta, por lo general sus dos extremos.
route_compare.name.definition: route_long_name of the GTFS feed (or the short name, or the label, when it has none), from transit_routes.geojson.
route_compare.name.method: Looked up by operator and route label in transit_routes.geojson.
route_compare.name.geography: Each bus route of the Route analysis (97 routes of 12 systems)
